criteria: A competitor could do the same next week without anything Archymedes holds
It leaves little behind, or only what is public or quick to rebuild
It leaves something a competitor would need months to rebuild, such as our own code, a signed release or a working process
It creates something a competitor cannot simply rebuild: outcome data from use, paid access enforced on our servers, owned IP or brand, or customer relationships
It strengthens a moat that compounds: every customer or use makes our data, trust or relationships harder to match

projects.gate: An integrator distribution agreement and authorized site access; field validation against incumbent management tools and operating costs.
projects.milestone: Long-term supported device integrations installed through repeat integrator customers, with vendor-cooperation records and explicit permission to retain a bounded deidentified corpus of confirmed device failures, false alarms and maintenance outcomes. Each authorized site contributes reviewed labels that improve fleet diagnostics and operating playbooks. Customer contracts and deployment history are maintained, not merely proposed.
projects.moat: Supported device integrations, integrator distribution and confirmed failure and maintenance histories
projects.name: Integrator-backed physical sensor reliability network
projects.offer: Per-site subscriptions sold through integrators, deployment and protocol maintenance.
projects.statusNote: Diagnoser prototype runs. 450 of 450 causes named on synthetic traces.

projects.buyer: Defense software integrators evaluating non-weapon enterprise and support applications
projects.gate: Domain evaluation partners, explicit data/model permissions, independent validation, confidentiality controls and a buyer who pays for evaluation outcomes rather than generic reports.
projects.milestone: A recurring evaluation service integrated with several authorized defense-software suppliers, with access to rights-cleared domain-specific held-out tasks that benchmark owners keep confidential. Explicit bounded permissions allow retention of deidentified evaluation failure categories and verified remediation outcomes. Independently reviewed evaluations, repeated outcomes and trusted customer relationships accumulate; no customer prompt/answer or classified-data pooling is assumed.
projects.moat: Confidential benchmarks, trusted independent evaluations and recurring supplier integrations
projects.name: Private defense AI evaluation network
projects.offer: Private evaluation integration, recurring evaluation contracts and supported local execution.
projects.statusNote: EvalEvidence and DataScope first passes, 13 engine tests each.

projects.buyer: Defense-installation energy and logistics equipment maintainers
projects.gate: Fleet and test-lab partners, reference-quality data and permission grants; long observation periods and strong existing vendors.
projects.milestone: A validated diagnostic workflow for one battery family across repeat fleet customers, with agreements covering historical telemetry, independent capacity/reference tests and bounded deidentified derived failure/warranty outcomes. Longitudinal aging observations, reference measurements and equipment integrations improve across permitted cohorts and connect to recurring maintenance decisions.
projects.moat: Longitudinal aging data, reference measurements and equipment-specific diagnostic models
projects.name: Battery degradation and field-outcome network
projects.offer: Per-fleet diagnostics subscriptions, reference testing and maintenance planning integrations.
projects.statusNote: Public aging data for 251 cells loaded (CC BY 4.0).

projects.buyer: Subsea cable operators and authorized infrastructure security teams
projects.gate: Cable-operator and sensing-hardware partners, real field validation, infrastructure-data protections and substantial deployment capital.
projects.milestone: An operator-contracted monitoring workflow with authorized access to existing cable sensing, site-specific calibration and operator-confirmed infrastructure events. Explicit rights permit bounded retained derived signatures and validated labels; unique installation access, local environmental history and repeated confirmed outcomes improve the service. Operators control raw infrastructure data and disclosures.
projects.moat: Operator access, installed sensing infrastructure and site-specific, confirmed event histories
projects.name: Operator-integrated subsea infrastructure condition service
projects.offer: Operator service contracts, sensing integration and reviewed infrastructure alerts.
projects.statusNote: Open-source threat picture with live AIS built. Needs operator fiber and DAS interrogators.

projects.buyer: Defense electronics suppliers, authorized distributors and inspection laboratories
projects.gate: Manufacturer/distributor and inspection-lab participation, authenticated claim sources and lawful data rights; physical verification cannot be replaced by a record checker.
projects.milestone: A recurring supplier/inspection workflow with direct verified manufacturer/distributor relationships, traceable lot and chain-of-custody records, and authorized laboratory inspection outcomes. Contracted participants can verify permitted claims; trusted cross-party history and bounded opt-in derived anomaly labels improve with continued use. A cryptographic ledger alone is not proof of a physical part or an asserted relationship.
projects.moat: Verified manufacturer relationships, chain-of-custody records and laboratory inspection outcomes
projects.name: Verified component provenance and inspection network
projects.offer: Participant verification/workflow subscriptions, integration and inspection coordination.
projects.statusNote: Research only. VisA PCB images identified (CC BY 4.0).

projects.buyer: Aerospace/defense component suppliers and their qualification customers
projects.gate: One qualified supplier and test-lab partner, bounded data-use agreements, independently measured usefulness; formal qualification remains with the authorized customer or body.
projects.milestone: A supported qualification workflow for one narrowly defined process family, integrated with repeat supplier customers and test laboratories, with verified process/lot/test outcomes and explicit rights to retain permitted derived statistics for validation. Accumulated accepted/rejected outcomes improve the reference corpus and shorten repeated evidence preparation. Customers retain their raw records and approval authority.
projects.moat: Supplier and test-lab integrations and accumulated qualification evidence
projects.name: Defense component qualification graph
projects.offer: Supported supplier integrations, evidence workflow subscriptions and reviewed qualification packages.

projects.buyer: Defense maintenance contractors for auxiliary power and logistics equipment
projects.gate: A maintenance partner with trustworthy failure/repair histories and explicit permitted reuse; competition from established predictive-maintenance vendors.
projects.milestone: A deployed supported workflow across repeat maintenance customers for one equipment class, with agreed access to historical condition and maintenance records and bounded permission to retain deidentified derived fault/repair outcomes. Maintenance-confirmed labels, equipment-specific integrations and repeat longitudinal observations improve estimates across permitted cohorts. No right to pool raw records is assumed.
projects.moat: Equipment-specific maintenance histories, confirmed repairs and embedded customer workflows
projects.name: Fleet reliability and repair-outcome network
projects.offer: Per-equipment or fleet subscription, integration and recurring outcome review.

question: How much harder to copy would `option` make Archymedes: data that compounds with use, paid access enforced on our servers, signed releases people can trust, ownership of code, IP and brand, or customer relationships a competitor cannot take?
